encounters.cc: Neck pain radiating down left arm with numbness in thumb and index finger

lines: Neck pain radiating down left arm with numbness in thumb and index finger

The patient, a 59-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, diabetic nephropathy, and recently diagnosed Multiple System Atrophy, presents to the Orthopedic Surgery clinic with a 6-week history of neck pain that radiates down his left arm.
He describes the pain as a sharp, burning sensation that worsens with neck extension and turning his head to the left.
He also reports numbness in his left thumb and index finger.
- Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
His medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 60
Smoking: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
On physical examination, there is decreased sensation to light touch over the left thumb and index finger, and weakness in the left biceps and wrist extensors.
The biceps reflex is diminished on the left side.
Cervical spine MRI reveals degenerative changes with osteophyte formation and foraminal narrowing at the C5-C6 level.

encounters.cc: Progressive right hand weakness with difficulty performing fine motor tasks

lines: Progressive right hand weakness with difficulty performing fine motor tasks

The patient presents with new right hand symptoms, returning six months after orthopedic evaluation for left neck pain with arm numbness, in the setting of multiple system atrophy and diabetic nephropathy.
He reports 3-month progressive right hand weakness with difficulty buttoning shirts and dropping objects.
He denies pain, numbness, or tingling in affected hand.
- Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
His past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 60
Smoking: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
On physical examination, the patient has normal muscle bulk in both upper extremities.
When asked to outstretch his arms with palms up and eyes closed, his right arm drifts downward and the palm pronates.
His grip strength is 4/5 on the right and 5/5 on the left.
Reflexes are 3+ in the right biceps and brachioradialis, and 2+ on the left.
There is no sensory deficit noted.
Babinski sign is upgoing on the right side.
